smells.label: Long Method
smells.description: A function/method body exceeds 30 lines of code, making it hard to understand and test.
smells.rationale: Long methods do too much. Break them into smaller, focused functions with descriptive names.

smells.label: God Class
smells.description: A class has more than 10 methods or 20 attributes, accumulating too many responsibilities.
smells.rationale: God Classes violate the Single Responsibility Principle. Split them into cohesive, focused classes.

smells.label: Dead Code
smells.description: Functions or variables are declared but never called/used anywhere in the codebase.
smells.rationale: Dead code adds confusion and maintenance burden. Remove it or mark it with a deprecation note.

smells.label: Long Parameter List
smells.description: A function has more than 4 parameters, making calls difficult to read and error-prone.
smells.rationale: Group related parameters into a data class or object to simplify function signatures.

smells.label: Duplicate Code
smells.description: Identical or near-identical code blocks (5+ lines) appear in two or more places.
smells.rationale: Duplication means bugs must be fixed in multiple places. Extract shared logic into a reusable function.

smells.label: Magic Number
smells.description: Numeric literals are used directly in code instead of being assigned to named constants.
smells.rationale: Named constants explain intent. Replace 86400 with SECONDS_PER_DAY to make code self-documenting.

smells.label: Deeply Nested Code
smells.description: Control structures are nested more than 4 levels deep, creating hard-to-follow logic.
smells.rationale: Use early returns (guard clauses) and extracted methods to flatten deeply nested control flow.
